title: Live Again
text: The backing chorus at the end.

title: Great Is
text: The chorus of this song is like a forceful anthem. It takes you into the bridge transition, which also occurs at the end of the song, that has this cool off-beat part each measure (see 2:48). Finally, if you’re a fan of Coheed and Cambria, you’ll hear that the singer’s voice Jenna Barrientes sounds a lot like Claudio Sanchez in some parts, but almost exactly in the run at 2:44.

title: Mutiny
text: Had this album playing on repeat the entire summer of 2010. One of my favorite albums the whole way through.

title: Reach
text:
The chorus hits you like a ton of bricks.

“Living in my head…”

title: Touch of Heaven
text: The overlap of Christian music with post rock becomes more apparent the more I listen to both. The melodic sounds, slow build ups, and explosive climax. This song has three of them. The last one culminates after about 10 minutes of soft, melodic worship into a build up and release that I’d say brings me closer to God than any other song I’ve listened to (see my point about this here). Towards the end of the build up at the 23:25 mark, the camera goes to the drummer–there’s something about his face, his passion, that makes me look forward to that specific shot everytime I watch it. It’s the best video on the internet. Period. Watch and immerse yourself for all 23 minutes and you’ll see why.

title: I Am A River
text: This song is the closer on Sonic Highways, one of my favorite albums. It’s basically perfect–the build-up and powerful ending. It has the same energy/feel as Wheels, which is among my favorite songs of all-time (and also on this list here). Strangely, I’m not actually that into Foo Fighters. This album (+ Wheels) are really the only stuff of theirs I can get hooked on. My Hero and some of their other hits are decent but I don’t go out of my way to listen.

title: New Thing Coming
text: Change in tone from intro to other part.

title: Been So Good
text: Guitar part in bridge.

title: History
text: The best song on the album.

title: Blinded
text: Favorite song from who I consider tied for the #1 spot as my favorite band. Different words in each chorus. The ride symbol during the chorus.

title: My Instincts are the Enemy
text: My favorite song of all time. Even though “Never Meant” is considered thee all-time classic emo song (and don’t get me wrong, I absolutely love it), I actually prefer American Football’s comeback albums from 2016 and 2019. It’s something about the maturity of the music/lyrics that is much deeper (and relatable) at this stage of life. In the 1999 album, the songs reflected their struggles as they were at the time of their college-aged selves. Now they’re all 40+ year old dads still singing about life, but it dwarfs the silly issues they thought they had when they were younger. You also notice that in the original album cover they’re looking at the house from the outside looking in. In 2016 it’s looking from the inside looking out. This song in particular sticks out, first of all, because of the lyrical content, which to me just feels all too relatable. But also because of the bridge (see 2:28). It doesn’t seem that special at first, but the technicality of the timing of the guitar part as the bass comes in just sounds like something you don’t hear too often. Like they have two different time signatures running together, which sounds contradicting and confusing, but it ends up being the perfect build up to the ending.

title: Turnstile
text: Vasudeva is one of my favorite (if not thee favorite) mathy post rock bands. If there is one word to describe their music, it is “hope”. There is a relentless optimism in the sounds, yet it has deep emotion. This is particularly noticable when you listen to No Clearance (the name of this album) all the way through. The song “Turnstile” is my favorite on the album, and part of it is how it transitions from “Slowboy” as it feels like they just needed to continue even though the song is over. Like your optimism starts fading so they say, “we’re not done yet” and give you a little bit more.

title: Wheels
text: A song full of meaning and purpose that just brings on a new bout of hope and optimism while reaching deep in your soul. The power that which the music is delivered in combination with the lyrics gives you chills. And it all sort of culiminates at the end when you get the drum fill leading into the last chorus that has overlayed guitar parts with the vocals on top. It’s like they did all these parts separately through the song, then do it all at once/together at the end for final bang, and then it’s over (see 3:57). It is in my top five (5) favorite songs of all time.

title: Death Of A Strawberry
text: Pretty much every Dance Gavin Dance album is gold (particularly those with Tilian, but Downtown Battle Mountain is also incredible). They have such a unique sound, and very technical instrumentally.

title: Some Will Seek Forgiveness, Others Escape
text: I’ve listened to Underoath since 6th or 7th grade. This is their best song on their best album (even though I definitely didn’t used to think that). Usually it’s refreshing nowadays when you see older bands from your younger days release comeback albums with a more Christian and/or mature tilt. Unfortunately it seems Underoath is taking the opposite approach and moving away from all that as they get older, which is disappointing and paradoxical.

title: Bubble Bath
text: Even though I’m a big math rock fan, I only recently discovered standards. All their albums are awesome and the fruit theme gives it an extra happy vibe that matches the music. But the part that makes them special is how technical the music actually is, yet it’s chill and relaxed enough that you could play it in any room. That is definitely not the case for all math rock. Bubble Bath sticks out for me because of its almost “cheesy” dance-like opening melody, but there’s this underlying emotion and fullness in the guitar. He’s not just playing it on one string–you can hear him hitting multiple strings as his fingers slide around. That lasts the whole song. But the part that really does it is the transition from the main melody to this other part (listen at 1:29), particularly where he does a little run half way through the measure. The other cool thing is how this run part only happens every other time (listen at 0:35).

title: Rejoice
text: She holds the “Rejoice” at the end of the song which adds so much more power and declaration to it than in the album version (see 2:58).

title: Cute Without The E
text: This is the toned-down acoustic version of the album version, but it’s one of the best live performances of any song. The reason it’s so good is because of just that: the small, intimate crowd makes it seem like everyone is singing along and performing together, which is explicit in this part. You can tell there’s just a lot of passion and nostalgia in the room the entire song. Also, the backing singer has an incredible voice.

title: Call To Arms
text: Drum part in bridge.

title: Strawberry Hill
text: One of my favorite bands ever. This song gives Foo Fighters vibes.

title: Reckless Love
text:
A while back I randomly stumbled on this reaction video of this Cory Asbury song, for whatever reason. After watching that, then proceeding to watch the entire original video above, I got hooked on this theme of live Christian rock performances that I now listen to regularly (e.g., Elevation Worship, Churchome, Bethel Music, TRIBL). The music and energy in this performance is obviously one reason why I like it, but what also makes it great is the topic of the song: The Parable of the Lost Sheep.

“Now the tax collectors and sinners were all gathering around to hear Jesus. 2 But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law muttered, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.” 3 Then Jesus told them this parable: 4 “Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it? 5 And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders 6 and goes home. Then he calls his friends and neighbors together and says, ‘Rejoice with me; I have found my lost sheep.’ 7 I tell you that in the same way there will be more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent.”

For some reason, this one hit home. So much so that I bought a picture representation of it to hang on my wall (and I’m not one to care much about decorating). Oh, and his Dave Matthews-esque vibe with a hoodie and Yankees hat singing about Jesus (even though Matthews doesn’t wear either of those that I’ve seen) made me like it even more.

title: Hospitality
text: This song sounds pretty average starting out, but it’s that build-up to the ending that’s great (see 3:07). So you have to listen to the whole thing to get to that point.

title: All That I’ve Got
text: I’ve been listening to this song pretty consistently since about 2006 (something about this one in particular distinctly reminds me of middle school), and it just never gets old.

title: Into Oblivion (Reunion)
text: The album this song is on came out in 2007, not too long after Hours, but something about it, and this song in particular, that sounds like many more years of maturity and optimism.

title: Iris
text: Obviously an all-time classic performance in the rain. What makes this version great is how he sings the chorus differently than the recorded version with much more power and depth, particularly “I just want you to know who I am”. That, plus the crowd interaction.

title: Idea Of You
text: “Idea Of You” is one of my favorite songs of all time. I still hold Dave Matthews Band as one of the (if not thee) best live performances I’ve ever seen. For the longest time this song was always so mysterious because it was only ever played live but never recorded on an album, so it was always a question of what it was. They would it at shows randomly but I think the lyrics would change and so it was just unpredictable and I could never find a consistent version of it. Finally, on their 2018 album “Come Tomorrow” they added a studio recording of it (see here). However, it’s hard to beat the live versions with this band, especially those with that red guitar.

title: Here as in Heaven
text: The title of this album is Evidence. I would argue that not only is this song about the evidence of God, but the song itself is too. I have this theory, stemming from the fact that you feel Him more or less with certain sounds, that there exists sounds that maximally elicit his presence. The closer you are to finding those sounds the more he is physically there with you. At some point, the music is him. The opposite is also true.

title: Arsonist Blues
text: I’d be surprised if someone knows this song/band…except Look Mexico. I stumbled on Summer Darling in a total coincidence: I had been listening to “Math is Everywhere” by Look Mexico for a few years, and then at some point I read that it was a cover (don’t remember where), so I dug around to find the original artist, and figured out it was Summer Darling. It turned out to be the last song on their first album from 2004. Then I started listening to this album and “Arsonist Blues” stuck out the most. It has late 90’s/early 2000’s summer nostalgia written all over it. The story, the sound, and the lyrics all make it seem like something we should have been listening to a long time ago.

title: Big Machine
text:
The best Goo Goo Dolls song. The lyrics and the story are filled with optimism and contentment.

“God it’s good to be alive.”


“You’re all I’m not. I don’t need what you ain’t got.”

Makes you appreciate the journey.
Then you’re hit by a classic Goo Goo Dolls chorus. Also the backing guitar with the weird octave chords playing, particularly in the second verse, make it more interesting. And then the overlay in the bridge/last chorus:

“God it’s good to be alive and I’m still here waiting for you.”

title: Can We Stay Like This
text: I really like this whole album. All The Time is another one of my favorites on it. This one though stands out though. The lyrics are so benign and vague (e.g., “I need you to know we’ve really got this now.”), but in a deep sense, and that’s why I like it for some reason.

title: Cold
text:
This played on the radio when I was a kid and it was always a good song. But now it hits different. The sound is great and the lyrics are deep. The best part is the bridge:

“I never really wanted you to see the screwed up side of me that I keep locked inside of me so deep. It always seems to get to me. I never really wanted you to go. So many things you should have known. I guess for me there’s just no hope. I never meant to be so cold”

Actually this whole album is really good. Some honorable mentions are “So Far Away” and “Colors”.

title: Machine
text:
Perdition is one of my favorite (if not thee favorite) screamo albums ever, the whole thing through. This song is probably my favorite on the album, because of the combination of the music, lyrics, and the way they’re sung. They make you visualize actual gears churning while hitting deep.

“Cause it was us rebuilding this machine.”

title: Life Support
text:
This is the perfect closer from their most recent full-length album from 2019. Just immediately the tone of the guitars are filled with deep emotion, which gets even more amplified as the bass and drums come in (see 0:54). As the vocals come in (see 2:03), the song feels like longing, contemplation and desperation, and that’s made explict with lines like:

“I’m looking for the words that I’ve lost on you. Been digging in the dirt. Now I’m buried in reminiscence.”

title: Enamor Me
text: This is one of my favorite albums, but Enamor Me is the song on it that you are looking forward to hearing.

title: Dandelion
text: Hard to single out just one song on this album (Nuet), so maybe I’ll add more. In this one, they basically follow the same thing the entire time, but just keep layering stuff on. I’d recommended putting this album on all the way through.

title: Stolen
text: Dusk and Summer is one of the best albums out there.

title: Holding On
text: This band as a whole is sort of mysterious and unique in their sound. The singer’s voice in this song is incredible, especially in the last chorus (see 3:15).

title: The Source
text: The voice is mesmerizing. Perfect introduction to the album.

title: Estate Sale
text: Tommy Boys is one of the most under-the-radar bands in pop/punk/math rock, probably because they just released one album in 2015 then I never heard from them again. The reason Estate Sale is especially great is because of this music video (above). If you know the album version, you’ll know that the three choruses are more or less the same. But in the music video at the 2:13 timepoint (in the third chorus) the singer emphasizes the “day” in “Saturday”, which honestly makes the whole song.
